effects: The signer sends `shares` vault share tokens (the vault contract itself as ERC-20, CSWUSDC) to the withdrawal queue, which spends the signer's share allowance to the queue.
The queue mints a new withdrawal NFT to `receiver`. The holder of that NFT is the only one who can later claim the underlying assets.
The underlying assets are not paid now. Their amount is set later by fill(), at the vault's redeem rate at that time.
The queue calls UniversalDelegator.sweepPending() as itself. This does not move the signer's assets.
formats.shown: Request queued withdrawal: queue N CSWUSDC shares from vault 0x9902…, with the withdrawal NFT sent to the receiver address.

findings.title: requestRedeem labels the receiver 'NFT recipient' and does not say this address gets the right to claim the assets.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol requestRedeem: `_mint(receiver, tokenId);`. claim: `if (ownerOf(tokenId) != msg.sender) revert NotTokenOwner();`. Descriptor: label "NFT recipient", interpolatedIntent "Queue {shares}, NFT to {receiver}". Cases 0 and 2 send the NFT to an address other than the signer.
findings.fix: Rename the label to "Withdrawal claim right (NFT) to". Change the interpolatedIntent to "Queue {shares} for withdrawal, claimable by {receiver}".

findings.title: requestRedeem cannot show the asset amount the signer later receives, because fill() sets it at a later rate.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol fill: `assets = IERC4626(vault).redeem(shares, address(this), address(this));` sets the cumulative asset checkpoints after the request. No calldata value fixes the amount the signer gets back.

effects: The signer must own withdrawal NFT `tokenId`. The NFT stays with the signer and is not burned.

The queue sends the filled, unclaimed part of the request to `receiver`, paid in the vault's underlying asset (vault.asset()). The amount comes from storage and can be zero or only part of the request.
The request's sharesClaimed goes up by the claimed shares, so this part of the NFT's claim right is used up.
formats.shown: Claim filled withdrawal for NFT #ID to the receiver address, with vault 0x9902… shown. No asset or amount is shown.

findings.title: claim does not name the asset paid out; 'Asset recipient' leaves the token the receiver gets unstated.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol claim: `IERC20(IERC4626(vault).asset()).safeTransfer(receiver, assets);`. Descriptor: intent "Claim filled withdrawal", field label "Asset recipient". Neither names the underlying token.
findings.fix: Name the vault's underlying asset in the intent or the label after you confirm it, for example "Claim filled USDC withdrawal" and the label "USDC recipient".

findings.title: claim cannot show the amount paid, because it comes from fill checkpoints in storage and may be partial or zero.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol claim: `(assets, shares) = claimable(tokenId);`. claimable caps `endShares` at `totalFilled()`, so only the filled part is paid.

findings.title: claim shows the withdrawal NFT ID raw, not as an NFT of this queue's collection.
findings.evidence: Descriptor field `#.tokenId` with format "raw", label "Withdrawal NFT ID". The queue contract is the ERC721 collection (WithdrawalQueue is ERC721Upgradeable).

couldNotCheck: VaultV2 at the constant 0x9902420048aEC155f1f1DF077f115595530Df216 has no source in the directory. I could not confirm that it is the queue's storage `vault`, that its share transferFrom in requestRedeem behaves as a plain ERC-20 transfer, or which token `asset()` returns for the claim payout.
